beats.narration_slice: At first, your hose might keep flowing from stored water pressure.
beats.visual: Cinematic charcoal-and-ink view of an unattended suburban backyard, a garden hose snaking across wet concrete and still spraying a weak arc into an overgrown flowerbed, with the empty house looming behind through gray haze.
beats.purpose: show that residual water pressure can keep a garden hose running briefly after people disappear
beats.visual_fingerprint: running green garden hose + weakening water arc + empty suburban backyard + low ground-level close-wide composition toward a dark vacant house
beats.continuity: enter the abandoned subject world directly through the running hose established by the question

beats.narration_slice: Within hours, unattended power grids would begin failing.
beats.visual: Wide upward charcoal view of an empty electrical substation at dusk, transformers and insulators receding beneath transmission towers while one isolated cold-amber utility light dims in the storm-gray air.
beats.purpose: show unattended electrical infrastructure beginning to fail within hours
beats.visual_fingerprint: silent electrical substation + dimming utility lamp + towering transmission lines + dramatic low-angle wide shot at gloomy dusk
beats.continuity: shift from household infrastructure to the larger utility network that supports it

beats.narration_slice: Many nuclear reactors would shut down automatically.
beats.visual: Distant elevated charcoal panorama of a nuclear power station under heavy overcast, cooling towers and containment buildings sitting still as steam output fades into a pale ink-wash sky, with no workers or vehicles present.
beats.purpose: show nuclear plants entering automatic shutdown without human operators
beats.visual_fingerprint: nuclear station exterior + fading steam plume + empty industrial grounds + elevated long-lens panoramic composition under flat overcast
beats.continuity: follow the grid failure into a major power facility responding automatically

beats.narration_slice: Cooling systems would still need power.
beats.visual: Simplified non-instructional charcoal cutaway of a reactor building focused on a dark cooling-water loop and pump chamber, with a small reservoir rendered in diluted blue-green ink and the surrounding machinery fading into soot shadow.
beats.purpose: explain that reactor cooling still depends on powered circulation systems after shutdown
beats.visual_fingerprint: simplified reactor cutaway + cooling-water loop + dormant pump chamber + centered sectional composition with blue-green water accent
beats.continuity: move from the plant exterior to the single support system that remains critical after shutdown

beats.narration_slice: Pets trapped indoors would face danger quickly.
beats.visual: Intimate charcoal interior of an abandoned apartment kitchen, a house cat standing beside an empty water bowl near a closed door, pale daylight filtering through blinds and casting long soft bars across the floor.
beats.purpose: show the immediate vulnerability of domestic pets trapped inside empty homes
beats.visual_fingerprint: solitary house cat + empty water bowl + closed apartment door + eye-level medium interior shot with striped window light
beats.continuity: pivot from infrastructure consequences to immediate effects on dependent animals

beats.narration_slice: Some farm animals would escape or starve.
beats.visual: Windblown charcoal farmyard seen from outside a broken fence, several cattle moving through a collapsed gate toward an empty field while a dark barn and scattered feed troughs sit abandoned in the background.
beats.purpose: show that livestock could either break free or lose access to human-provided food and care
beats.visual_fingerprint: cattle leaving through broken gate + abandoned feed troughs + open farm field + diagonal wide composition from behind a splintered foreground fence
beats.continuity: expand the animal consequence from enclosed household pets to livestock in larger human-managed spaces

beats.narration_slice: Without pumps, subways could begin flooding within days.
beats.visual: Deep one-point-perspective charcoal view down an empty subway tunnel, dark water already covering the rails and reflecting a few dying amber emergency lamps while stairs disappear into mist behind.
beats.purpose: show groundwater and seepage accumulating in subway systems once pumping stops
beats.visual_fingerprint: flooded subway rails + rising black water + dying emergency lamps + centered tunnel vanishing-point shot from near water level
beats.continuity: move from animal dependence to another hidden system that requires continuous powered maintenance

beats.narration_slice: Weeks later, weeds would spread across untended roads.
beats.visual: Top-down oblique charcoal streetscape weeks later, cracked asphalt overtaken by tufts of dead moss green weeds pushing through lane seams around a rusting abandoned bicycle and windblown debris.
beats.purpose: show vegetation beginning to reclaim paved urban surfaces within weeks
beats.visual_fingerprint: weeds splitting cracked roadway + abandoned bicycle + scattered debris + high oblique street shot dominated by branching green growth
beats.continuity: advance the timeline from days to weeks and shift from water intrusion to visible ecological reclamation

beats.narration_slice: Years later, weather would weaken empty buildings.
beats.visual: Low-angle charcoal view of a weather-beaten apartment block years later, rain streaks and cracks cutting across the facade as a section of roofline sags, vines cling to balconies, and storm haze erases the distant skyline.
beats.purpose: show long-term structural deterioration caused by weather and lack of maintenance
beats.visual_fingerprint: cracked apartment facade + sagging roofline + rain and climbing vines + low-angle architectural shot during a gray storm
beats.continuity: advance from early plant growth to years of combined weathering and biological decay

beats.narration_slice: Earth would keep going; our systems would not.
beats.visual: Quiet panoramic charcoal vista of a reclaimed city edge at dawn-gray light, trees and tall grasses overtaking a silent roadway in the foreground while corroded towers and collapsed utility lines recede into soft ink-wash mist.
beats.purpose: summarize the contrast between resilient natural processes and decaying human-built systems
beats.visual_fingerprint: reclaimed roadway + dense young trees + corroded skyline and fallen utility lines + wide contemplative horizon composition with misty atmospheric depth
beats.continuity: resolve the progression by widening from one failing building to the larger world continuing around abandoned infrastructure
